merger_name: Global Lithium Resources – IGO Nova Operation
merger_description:
GL1 HoldCo No 3 Pty Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of Global Lithium Resources Limited (**GL1**), is acquiring 100% of the issued share capital in IGO Nova Pty Ltd (**IGO Nova**) from IGO Nova Holdings Pty Ltd, a wholly owned subsidiary of IGO Limited (**IGO**) (the **Acquisition**).

A portion of the consideration for the Acquisition will be paid by way of scrip, which could see IGO own up to 13,333,333 shares in GL1. GL1 currently has approximately 277 million shares on issue. As such, even if the maximum amount of shares is issued, IGO will not own more than approximately 5% of GL1 immediately following the Acquisition.

GL1 (ASX: GL1) is an Australian lithium exploration and development company. It is primarily focused on advancing its 100% owned flagship Manna Lithium Project, located in the Goldfields region of Western Australia. GL1 is headquartered in West Perth, Western Australia.

IGO is an Australian mining and exploration company that discovers, develops and produces critical minerals, primarily lithium, nickel, copper and cobalt.

IGO Nova is the sole owner of the Nova Operation, an underground nickel, copper and cobalt mine in Western Australia’s Fraser Range. The Nova Operation also comprises a nickel-copper processing plant, a 500-bed operating camp and associated infrastructure (power station, a sealed runway, water treatment plant). The Nova Operation is at the end of its life and mining at the underground mine is expected to conclude by late 2026.

Following completion of the acquisition, the plant will be converted to process pegmatite ore mined from GL1’s Manna Lithium Project, avoiding the need for GL1 to build a new facility. The operating camp will provide accommodation for workers at both the Nova Operation and Manna Lithium Project.

events.title: Notification waiver determination published

determination_table_content.details:
In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information provided in the application, the ACCC
considers that the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material
lessening of competition, given:
a. there is no horizontal overlap between GL1 and IGO Nova in
the production of nickel, copper, cobalt or lithium in Australia
b. there is limited horizontal overlap between GL1 and IGO in
the production of lithium in Australia, and there are
alternative producers of lithium in Australia
c. the Acquisition is unlikely to result in any substantive change
of control of GL1.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Give that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined the Acquisition is not required to be notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s guidance on notification
waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
